subject: Bike Share Shiny App and UTF-8 Encoding Errors

messages.author: c6ca7877bef91eef
messages.subject: Bike Share Shiny App and UTF-8 Encoding Errors
parts:
I had earlier shared my work on visualizing NYC Bike Share network. Using a more general data source, I was able to create a Shiny App that can visualize bike sharing networks across the world.

Source: https://gist.github.com/ramnathv/6050562
Application: http://glimmer.rstudio.com/ramnathv/bikeshare

The only glitch I am running into is with regard to encoding. For some of the cities (especially with Spanish of French street names), the application quits without any meaningful error. When I test locally, I see the following message in the Chrome Console

WebSocket connection to 'ws://localhost:8100/' failed: Could not decode a text frame as UTF-8.

So, it seems to be an encoding issue. Now, in my R code, I tried to force convert data to UTF-8 using

bike = fromJSON(iconv(content(GET(url)), to = "UTF-8"))

But, that doesn't do the work, as the characters remain even after this statement.

So my question is what is the best way to deal with UTF-8 encoding errors. I have seen some solutions using JS, where the idea is to scrub the payload sent by server.R. But, I was more curious about R side solutions, as it would make my job easier.

Looking forward to comments/suggestions.

Best,
Ramnath

messages.author: c6ca7877bef91eef
messages.subject: Re: Bike Share Shiny App and UTF-8 Encoding Errors
parts:
I managed to solve the issue by locating the part of the json payload that did not have the correct encoding and force converting it. The relevant part of the code for those interested is

popup = iconv(whisker::whisker.render(
      '<b>{{name}}</b><br>
        <b>Free Docks: </b> {{free}} <br>
         <b>Available Bikes:</b> {{bikes}}
        <p>Retreived At: {{timestamp}}</p>'
   ), from = 'latin1', to = 'UTF-8')

This ensured that all the data sent to websockets was valid UTF-8, and this solved my issue.

If there are other solutions, I would like to hear about them.

Just for those who might randomly stumble on this thread from a Google search, as I did, in my experience the R-ish way of doing this is using:

enc2utf8(x)

I tried many other things such as iconv(x) with no success.
